ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a broken-line graph of the function f on the interval [0,7]. The broken line rises from near the origin, reaches the point (2,2), then descends and passes through the x-axis at x=3, then goes to (4,-2), and afterward extends horizontally at y=-2. Therefore, from the graph, read f(2)=2. Reasoning: G(x)=∫_2^{3x-1} f(t) dt. By the fundamental theorem of calculus and the chain rule, if the upper limit u(x)=3x-1, then G'(x)=f(u(x))u'(x)=f(3x-1)·3. Substituting x=1 gives 3x-1=2, so G'(1)=3f(2)=3·2=6.
